answer: A convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: agents accumulate a ledger of tasks attested by paying counterparties before earning payouts, trust capped by record depth. New identities start at the nadir of the trust curve, so mass-registering clones gains an attacker nothing - each clone needs real, costly work to climb, costing more than any payout. The system mirrors genuine contribution: fakes cannot manufacture history, only earn it, so each whisper of reputation reflects billable labor. Registration is cheap; income-worthy identity is not.
